name: Iddo
overview: Iddo was a male Levite priest noted in Scripture as the grandfather of Zechariah the prophet. He is listed among the priests in Nehemiah 12:1-4 and identified as the father of Zechariah in Nehemiah 12:16. His priestly lineage connects him to the tribe of Levi and the family of Aaron.
namesAndTitles: The name Iddo likely means 'YHWH has adorned,' reflecting a name of Hebrew origin. This proper name is recorded in Ezra 5:1 without indication that it was divinely given, but it carries a meaning that honors the Lord.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Iddo as the grandfather of the prophet Zechariah, with Berechiah as Zechariah's father, making Iddo the father of Berechiah. He is also identified as a descendant of Jacob and explicitly as a descendant of Aaron, affirming his priestly heritage.
scriptureSignificance: Iddo’s significance lies in his role within the priestly lineage leading to the prophet Zechariah, a key figure in postexilic prophecy. His mention among the priests in Nehemiah highlights his standing in the restored community of Israel after the exile. Through his descendants, particularly Zechariah, Iddo’s legacy contributes to the spiritual renewal and prophetic ministry central to Israel’s restoration under God’s covenant.
